- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent price surged.
- Underestimates volatility in mid-to-late forecast horizon; increase forecast variance or add upward bias for days 15–25 if sentiment remains neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of historical prices.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., +15–20% above true value) — apply decay factor of 0.95 per day to correct for momentum overestimation.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to recognize it — add a 3-day lagged correction rule: if day 1–3 are high, reduce forecast by 2–5% on day 4+.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation; if recent 7-day average is rising, cap forecast growth at 3–5% above that average to prevent over-optimism.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model tends to ignore macro event context — if official event (e.g., policy change, auction) is known, adjust forecast downward 2–5% for 3–5 days post-event.
